- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if recent price is falling.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the 10–15 day horizon after strong upward sentiment; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- Model overestimates in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; apply downward correction of 1–2% if sentiment < 0.33.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >1.5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1.5–2% above prior peak.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model tends to ignore it; apply slight upward bias to counteract.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers model lag; forecast should adjust 1–2 days ahead of true reversal.
